description: Eight sine waves at one frequency, each a further eighth of a cycle behind the last, usable as a bank of slow modulators or as an oscillator

params.text: Sets the frequency; what its travel covers depends on the range switch
Chooses the range: LFO, where the knob spans 0.01Hz to 100Hz, or OSC, where it spans four octaves either side of C4 at 261.63Hz

inputs.text: Adds to the frequency; in LFO it multiplies the rate by ten for every 5V, and in OSC it raises the pitch an octave per volt

outputs.text: A sine at the set frequency, ±5V, taken as the reference the other seven are measured from
The same sine an eighth of a cycle behind the first
The same sine a quarter of a cycle behind the first
The same sine three eighths of a cycle behind the first
The same sine half a cycle behind the first, which is the first one turned upside down
The same sine five eighths of a cycle behind the first
The same sine three quarters of a cycle behind the first
The same sine seven eighths of a cycle behind the first

notes: the eight outputs are one wave read at eight points, so they hold their spacing however the frequency is changed.
the lamp is lit while the first output is above 0V, which makes it a slow blink in the LFO range and a steady glow in the OSC range.
the frequency is worked out differently in each range, so flipping the switch moves the pitch a long way rather than stepping it.
